A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Generalized Random Forests using Fixed-Point Trees. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support a reliable comparison despite changed pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original correlation-sensitivity experiments, VCM and HTE simulations, and California housing analyses, including timing and estimation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and analyses in Sections 3, 6–7 and the appendices, including the housing timing results in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 5 revises the specified accelerated parent update: v2 Equation 27 becomes a positive parent-sample average in v3 Equation 28, and the line-search formula changes. These are localized computational-formula corrections; the overall fixed-point/CART procedure and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Changes to the implementation are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four VCM settings, five HTE settings, correlated-regressor scenario, and California housing data. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: GRF-grad remains the evaluated comparator for GRF-FPT throughout the corresponding simulations and housing analysis. No comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C/F retain the same sample sizes, target dimensions, forest sizes, MSE evaluation, single-tree sampling options, and housing preprocessing and defaults.

E4.justification: The correlated-regressor stability analysis in Figure 1, computational scaling analyses, and housing case study are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 6 retains 40 replications for MSE evaluation, with unchanged distribution plots in Figures 10 and 19. Repetition information and percentile-band reporting for Figure 1 also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The result plots and reported findings are unchanged. Table 4 still reports housing training times of 19.1 seconds for GRF-grad and 12.6 seconds for GRF-FPT, with a 1.52 speedup factor.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1 and Appendix B.3 redefine the radius over parent P instead of child Cj. Section 5 revises Jacobian and pseudo-outcome signs and restores the averaging factor in the OLS expression. The assumptions, asymptotic guarantees, and proof strategy are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim faster, more stable tree construction without sacrificing estimation accuracy or GRF consistency and asymptotic normality. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contribution scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of Jacobian instability, dimensionality-dependent computational savings, comparable accuracy, and applicability remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or interpretation is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendices C/F retain the same implementation interfaces, code and data links, sampling options, and housing processing instructions. Section 5's added matrix notation explains the existing centering operation.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationship to Athey et al.'s GRF framework and classical fixed-point methods.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct abstract wording, clarify the matrix notation in Section 5, and replace the erroneous 'Appendix 10' reference with 'Appendix D'. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained, with equation formatting and appendix float placement changes. For example, Table 4 moves after Figure 20 and shares the final page with Figure 21. The displays are not redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical precision through the corrected OLS averaging factor, more consistent Jacobian signs, and parent-node radius definition, while clarifying notation and repairing a cross-reference. These are useful localized improvements; the empirical evidence and theoretical guarantees remain unchanged.
